title: Savings & Money Market Accounts: Capacity Left Under the Per-Cycle Maximum of Excess Fees
content:
The tier of each Savings & Money Market Accounts product puts a ceiling on how many excess withdrawal fees a single statement cycle can bear. This page defines how much of that cap is still available in a cycle being squared against its counted withdrawals.

## Rule

**Each fee entry uses up the cap.** Every excess withdrawal fee entry posted in the cycle is counted toward the tier's per-cycle maximum, refunded or not, and whatever the ground of any refund. This is the same tally the cycle's own count of excess fees keeps.

**Capacity left.** The number of further excess fees the cycle can still take is the tier's per-cycle maximum less the number of such entries. It never drops below none.

**Fee entries must match the cycle.** The policy is applied only when the cycle's fee entries are consistent in their dating, as their posting dates and statement cycle labels show. A fee entry whose posting date lies inside the cycle, meaning on any day from the one following the prior closing date up to and including this cycle's closing date, must be labelled with this cycle; and an entry labelled with this cycle must have a posting date inside it. The entries of the cycle are then exactly those its own tally counts. Where this fails, the policy squares nothing.

## Worked examples (hypothetical cycles, per-cycle maximum assumed to be 6)

| Excess fee entries in the cycle | Of which refunded | Capacity left |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | none | 4 |
| 3 | 1, bank error | 3 |
| 6 | 2, courtesy | none |
| 7 | none | none, never below none |

## Points of judgement

**Does a refunded fee hand its place under the cap back?** No. A refund, on any ground, leaves the entry counted toward the maximum.
